adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:440 — Unsubscribe is a state-mutating GET with no CSRF token or recipient-bound key (contrast `put t/:topic_id/mute` and DigestUnsubscribeKey), so any third-party page embedding ``, a browser prefetch, or a cookie-bearing link scanner silently mutes/downgrades the logged-in user's topic notification level.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two GET routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) mapped to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, and that action *mutates state* by finding `TopicUser` for `current_user`, changing `tu.notification_level`, and calling `tu.save!`. Since it’s a GET (and the diff shows no per-recipient token/key in the URL or any CSRF-style verification in the action), it is vulnerable to CSRF-style triggering via third-party embeds/prefetch/link scanners that send cookies, causing silent notification-level changes for logged-in users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — TopicUser.find_by` returns nil for any logged-in user without a row for that topic (URL is guessable, not just from email), and line 107 then raises NoMethodError -> 500 instead of using `TopicUser.change` which creates the row.

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — Toggle is not idempotent and semantically mismatched: watching/tracking->regular (user still gets reply/mention emails despite page and email saying "stop receiving notifications"), regular->muted, muted->muted; a page refresh (URL stays `/unsubscribe`), double-click, or prefetch+click walks a watching user all the way to muted.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the notification level change is implemented as a toggle: `if tu.notification_level > ...[:regular]` then set to `:regular`, else set to `:muted` (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb). This makes the GET `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` endpoint non-idempotent: a user who is `:watching`/`:tracking` becomes `:regular` on first hit, then `:muted` on a second hit (refresh/double-click/prefetch). It also conflicts with the client copy in `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` (“stop receiving notifications...”), since `:regular` is not “no notifications” and still allows some notifications.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the code updates `TopicUser.notification_level` via `tu.notification_level = ...` followed by `tu.save!` instead of calling `TopicUser.change(...)`. The diff shows `TopicUser.change` is responsible for publishing `MessageBus.publish("/topic/#{topic_id}", { notification_level_change: ... }, ...)` when `attrs[:notification_level]` is set, and that publish will not happen in the controller path as written. The parts of the finding about `notifications_changed_at` / `notifications_reason_id` are not verifiable from this diff, but the missing MessageBus publish (and thus potential stale client state in already-open tabs) is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:96 — ensure_logged_in` on a non-XHR HTML GET means a logged-out recipient (typical on mobile mail clients) gets the generic not-found/403 page with no login redirect or return-to, and when they do log in the link acts on whichever account is active (shared device / forwarded email), not the addressed recipient.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a per-topic unsubscribe link in emails (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) that points to `/t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` without any per-recipient token. The new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action is protected by `ensure_logged_in` and then mutates `TopicUser` based solely on `current_user` (`TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` then toggles `notification_level`). adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, the logic is indeed a toggle-like rule: it sets `notification_level` to `:regular` when the current level is `> :regular` (e.g., tracking/watching), otherwise it sets it to `:muted` (regular→muted, muted→muted). The action name `unsubscribe` does not make that intended semantics obvious, and there’s no inline comment or extracted model method to explain why “unsubscribe” sometimes means “downgrade to regular” instead of always muting. This is a diff-grounded maintainability/clarity concern rather than a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 — unsubscribe_link` now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, making it an undocumented required companion of MessageBuilder's `add_unsubscribe_link: true` (I18n raises on missing interpolation), while the List-Unsubscribe header at message_builder.rb:107 still points at user_preferences_url; the option contract and header are now inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true it always does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` and `template_args` only includes defaults like `user_preferences_url` plus whatever the caller passes via `@opts`. There is no default `unsubscribe_url`, so any existing call site that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not provide `unsubscribe_url` will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at runtime. This is a correctness break introduced by the locale change (some call sites/specs were updated in the diff, but the contract change is real). The finding’s additional claim about the List-Unsubscribe header still pointing at `user_preferences_url` is not verifiable from the shown diff context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/app-route-map.js.es6:13 — Ember route is named `topicUnsubscribe` (top-level, files named topic-unsubscribe.*) but its template lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which only resolves via the resolver's decamelize+slash fallback; naming is inconsistent with the sibling `topic.*` nested routes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a top-level route `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)` (app-route-map.js.es6) and corresponding JS files named `topic-unsubscribe.*`, but the template is added at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` (i.e., `topic/unsubscribe`, which conventionally matches a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route). For a route named `topicUnsubscribe`, Ember would normally resolve `topic-unsubscribe` (dasherized) rather than `topic/unsubscribe`, so this mismatch is likely to cause the route to render without the intended template unless an undocumented resolver fallback exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — unsubscribe` mutates TopicUser.notification_level on a plain GET (routes.rb:440-441); Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, so any third-party page (``) or a cookie-carrying link prefetch/preview can silently step a logged-in user's level down to regular/muted; do the change via PUT/XHR from the Ember confirmation page and make the GET read-only.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action that **mutates state** (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`) and is wired up to **GET** routes (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` in `config/routes.rb`). Rails’ CSRF protection typically does not require/validate tokens on GET requests, so this creates a CSRF-able state change via e.g. an embedded image or link prefetch. The controller also `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`, making it accessible as a normal GET. This is a real security defect introduced by the diff.
